content.welcome:
Welcome to the City of Burton

Welcome, neighbor! The City of Burton, formerly Burton Township, was established in 1972. Through the years our city has grown in many ways, making it a great place to live, work, and raise your family.

This guide is your one-stop shop for City of Burton information — administrative staff, city council and meeting schedules, waste pickup, recycling, and permits for burning and dumping. If you have questions, contact City Hall Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. at (810) 743-1500.

— Mayor Duane Haskins

City Offices

Burton City Hall — 4303 S. Center Rd., Burton, MI 48519 Hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Mayor's Office, Assessor's Office, Clerk's Office, Controller's Office, Human Resources, and the Treasurer's Office (invoices, water, sewer & tax bills).

Department of Public Works (DPW) — 4093 Manor Dr., Burton, MI 48519 Hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. Building, Code Enforcement, Engineering, Major & Local Roads, Planning & Zoning, and Utilities Service.

City offices are on S. Center Rd., north of Maple Rd. and south of Bristol Rd. Main line: (810) 743-1500 · Fax: (810) 743-5060 · burtonmi.gov
content.trash-recycling:
Curbside service is provided by EMTERRA — 1606 E. Webster Rd., Flint, MI 48505 · (810) 667-4885. Garbage, recycling, and yard waste are all collected on the same day, and everything must be at the edge of the road (outside the ditch line) by 6:00 a.m.

Not sure which day is yours? See the Pickup Schedule section to look up your street.

Garbage

  • Unlimited bags within reason, 35 gallons or less, properly contained and tied. No small grocery bags (they're treated as loose trash).
  • Trash must be bagged, not loose in containers.
  • In winter, don't let cans fill with water — frozen bags can't be collected.
  • Each household gets one free dump permit per month (see Permits).
  • You may set out one large item per week on your normal trash day if it's under 50 lbs and two people can lift it. A whole-house clean-out requires a dump permit from City Hall.

Accepted large items: couches, chairs, tables, TVs, washers, dryers, stoves, box springs (fabric items must be dry — cover with clear plastic if raining); dried-out latex paint cans (lid off); carpet (rolled/tied, under 4 ft, 45 lbs or less, max 8 rolls/week); clean, bug-free mattresses (bagged if dirty or wet). Refrigerators, freezers, and A/C units are collected once Freon is removed by a licensed company and tagged with the removal date.

Not accepted: oil paint (hazardous), chest freezers, cast iron tubs, cement/concrete/ rocks, tires, nails or screws, and demolition lumber. Bundle material no larger than 4 ft × 1 ft; larger amounts are industrial refuse and must be removed by the resident or their contractor.

Recycling

Picked up the same day as trash, out by 6:00 a.m. The City sells recycling containers for $7.00 each, and offers free stickers to use your own lidded/handled container (35 gallons max, under 50 lbs). Place recycling on the opposite side of the driveway from the trash, label facing the road. No plastic bags.

Yard Waste

Collected the same day as trash, first full week of April through the last full week of November (weather permitting). Use two-ply paper yard-waste bags (from grocery or hardware stores) or your own 35-gallon (under 50 lb) container with free yard-waste stickers from City Hall (limit four per household). No plastic bags.

Includes: lawn clippings, brush, thatch, leaves, border edgings, tree & plant pruning, vines & garden clearings. Brush/branches: under 2 inches in diameter, bundled in 4 ft lengths. Christmas trees are collected through the end of January (bare — no ornaments or hooks). Not yard waste: gravel, dirt, sod, rock, stones, stumps, cement.

Bulk Items

One bulk item per week, collected the same day as trash. Examples: stoves, A/C units, refrigerators, bed frames, hot water heaters, water softeners, garbage disposals, freezers, dishwashers, dryers, humidifiers, treadmills, washers. Freon appliances need the Freon removed by a licensed company and tagged with the date.

  • Cardboard: flattened, bundled, tied with twine; no longer/wider than 3 ft.
  • Computers: one complete unit (monitor, desktop, printer) free; extra or larger office equipment over 50 lbs is handled as a bulk item.
  • Tires & auto parts: not accepted. For tires, contact Environmental Rubber Recycling Inc. at (810) 789-1222.
  • Non-collectible: animal waste, dead animals, lumber, demolition material, insecticides, oil/gas/propane tanks, antifreeze, concrete, gravel, dirt, sod, rock, stumps, car parts, batteries, riding mowers, bricks, roofing shingles, and paint cans with paint still in them.

Hazardous & Electronic Waste

Handled by the Genesee County Metropolitan Planning Commission. Check dates and locations at (810) 762-7744 or gcmpc.org. Anything labeled toxic, corrosive, flammable, or reactive is hazardous and needs special disposal.

content.permits:
Dump Permits

Dump permits (with full regulations) are available at Burton City Hall. Each Burton household is entitled to one (1) free dump permit per month. You must reside in the household as your principal residence and show proof of residency (valid ID, water bill). Only Burton residents may request a permit, and it must be obtained at City Hall.

  • A permit covers materials from your own home only — proper ID is required at the landfill.
  • One permit equals a standard pickup-truck load, under 1,000 lbs. Larger loads are charged the difference (and you may be asked to drive back). A reflective vest is required to enter the landfill.
  • Good for small amounts of household demolition and household refuse. Michigan law requires a tarp over each load. You must be fully unloaded and out before closing.
  • Freon must be removed by a licensed company and tagged with the removal date.
  • If you can't use the permit within the calendar month, return it to City Hall for a new one. Lost permits are not replaced.

Disposal site: Brent Run Landfill, 8335 Vienna Rd., Montrose, MI 48457 — open Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m. Questions: (810) 639-3077. (The landfill is outside the city, so it isn't pinned on the map — use the map's "Dump Permits" listing for directions.)

Burning Permits

It is illegal to burn in the City of Burton without a permit. Permits are issued for one- and two-family residential dwellings only (no commercial), and your driver's license must match the burning address. Get permits from the Fire Department, City Hall, or burtonmi.gov. Keep your permit on hand whenever you burn.

General rules: keep an adequate fire line around the burn area, always attend the fire, and keep a garden hose or other means of extinguishment on hand. Barrel burning is not permitted. Don't burn when it's windy. Smoke and ash must not be a nuisance to neighbors.

Open Burning

  • Brush, tree limbs, and garden debris only — no leaves, grass, or building materials.
  • Four (4) three-consecutive-day open-burn permits per household per year.
  • Stay 50 feet from any building or structure; pile no larger than 4 ft × 5 ft.
  • Fires must be out by sundown. Extensions may be granted by calling the Fire Department or City Hall within 30 days of issuance.

Recreational Burning

  • Seasoned wood only — no leaves, grass, garden debris, or building materials.
  • Annual permit, good through December 31 regardless of issue date.
  • Stay 25 feet from any building or structure; pile no larger than 3 ft × 3 ft.
  • Fires must be out by 1:00 a.m.

Violating these rules may result in a revoked permit, suspended burning privileges, and being charged for the cost of the fire run. Any property loss from your burn is your responsibility.

Utility Billing

The Treasurer's Office at City Hall handles water, sewer, tax, and invoice billing. Call (810) 743-1500 with questions.

Automatic Bill Payment

The City offers automatic bill payment for utility customers — a convenient way to pay your utility bill on time and avoid delinquent fees, at no cost to you. Payments are deducted from your checking or savings account on the 15th of the month when your balance is due.

To enroll, complete the Utility Payment Automatic Transfer Authorization form and return it to:

City of Burton, 4303 S. Center Rd., Burton, MI 48519

You can get the authorization form from the Treasurer's Office or in the official Resident Packet (use the "Download the official packet (PDF)" link in this guide). For details, call the City Treasurer's Office at (810) 743-1500.
content.property-taxes:
Look up a property, assessment, or tax bill

The City of Burton publishes assessing and tax records through BS&A Online. You can search any property and view assessment details, current and past tax bills, building-department records, and sales history — and pay a tax bill online:

  • Burton property & tax search (BS&A Online) — Assessing Search, Current Tax Search, Building Department Search, Property Sale Search, and online payment.

Records are maintained by the City and updated regularly. For questions about your assessment or tax bill, contact the City at (810) 743-1500:

  • Assessor (Ann Abbey) — assessed/taxable value, exemptions, property characteristics.
  • Treasurer (Alice Bryce) — tax bills, payments, due dates.

City offices are at Burton City Hall; see burtonmi.gov for hours and department pages.

Understanding your tax bill

Property tax in Michigan is calculated on a property's taxable value, using a rate measured in mills.

  • One mill = $1 of tax for every $1,000 of taxable value. For example, at a rate of 4 mills, a property with $50,000 of taxable value owes $50,000 ÷ 1,000 × 4 = $200 per year. (Burton's actual city operating millage is shown on the Finances dashboard in this app.)
  • Taxable value is not the same as market value — or even the sale price. When you buy a home, its taxable value is set to that year's State Equalized Value (about half of market value). After that, Michigan's Proposal A caps how much the taxable value can rise each year (the lower of 5% or inflation) until the property is sold, so over time taxable value usually falls below market value.
  • Your total rate combines several millages — city operating, plus schools, the county, libraries, and voter-approved millages. The Finances dashboard breaks down the City's portion.

Why the city rate is below its maximum

You may notice the City's operating millage is levied below its authorized maximum. That gap is largely the Headlee Amendment (Michigan Constitution, Article IX, §31): when a community's total taxable value grows faster than inflation, the maximum millage a local government may levy is automatically "rolled back" so that property-tax revenue grows no faster than inflation. Voters can restore a rolled-back rate with a "Headlee override," but absent that, the cap ratchets down.

Learn more:

  • What is the Headlee Amendment? (MSU Extension)
  • Michigan property taxes (State of Michigan)
content.elections:
Register, check your status, and find where to vote

Michigan's official Voter Information Center is the one place to handle almost everything about voting — registration, your polling location, your sample ballot, and absentee ballots:

  • Michigan Voter Information Center (MVIC) — register or update your address, check your registration, find your polling place, view your sample ballot, apply for an absentee ballot, and track your ballot. For current and upcoming election dates, see MVIC (dates change, so we link the official source rather than list them here).

Michigan offers same-day registration: you can register in person at your city clerk's office through Election Day with proof of residency.

Local election help

  • City of Burton Clerk (Racheal Boggs) — city election questions, in-person registration, and absentee ballot requests for Burton residents. Burton City Hall, (810) 743-1500.
  • Genesee County Elections Division — administers federal, state, and local elections in the county. Elections office: 1101 Beach St., Flint, MI 48502.
  • Genesee County voter information — county-level voter resources.

Vote by mail (absentee)

Any registered Michigan voter may request an absentee ballot — no reason required. Request it through MVIC or directly from the Burton City Clerk, then return your completed ballot to the Clerk by mail or to a designated drop box. Track its status on MVIC.
content.transit:
Getting around by bus

Public transit in Burton is provided by the Mass Transportation Authority (MTA) of Genesee County, based in Flint. MTA's fixed bus routes connect Burton with Flint and neighboring communities, and connect to the Flint transit center for transfers across the county.

Routes serving Burton

  • Route 15 — Burton–Davison
  • Route 9 — Lapeer Road
  • Route 11 — Fenton Road

Each route page has the current schedule and stops. Routes and times can change, so check the official MTA page before you travel. You can also see every MTA route that runs through Burton on the Map — open the layer control (top-right) and turn on Bus routes.

Plan a trip & fares

  • All routes & schedules
  • Fares
  • MTA Flint home — trip planning, curb-to-curb service, senior and disability options, and other programs.
  • Customer service: (810) 767-0100.
content.roads:
Live traffic & construction (state routes)

For real-time lane closures, construction, and traffic on the state highways through and around Burton — I-69, I-475, and M-54 (Dort Highway) — use MDOT's live map:

  • MDOT Mi Drive live traffic & construction map

Mi Drive covers Interstate, US, and M (state) routes only — not city or county streets.

City street projects

The City maintains local roads through its Major Streets and Local Streets funds (see the Finances dashboard in this app for how those are budgeted). The Fiscal Year 2026-2027 budget includes road, intersection, and sidewalk work along these corridors:

  • Belsay Road, Bristol Road, Maple Avenue, Genesee Road (incl. a sidewalk project), Court Street, North Grand Traverse Street, Covert Road, and Hemphill Road
  • Intersection upgrades at Bristol/Belsay (roundabout) and Bristol/Fenton
  • The Iron Belle Trail non-motorized path

These are budgeted projects, not a live closure schedule, and their timing can shift. For the status of a current local road project or to report a road concern, contact the Department of Public Works at (810) 742-9230 (DPW page).

Neighborhood paving

Several neighborhoods are repaved through special-assessment paving districts funded by the benefiting property owners. Questions about a paving district or assessment: contact City Hall at (810) 743-1500.
content.help:
Food assistance

If you need food, help is available locally.

The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan is an equal-opportunity provider that partners with a network of more than 700 hunger-relief partners across 22 counties.

  • Food assistance line: (810) 239-4441
  • Dial 2-1-1 for other available resources
  • Address: 2300 Lapeer Road, Flint, MI 48503
  • Food pantry calendar: fbem.org

Food pantries in the City of Burton

  • Harris Memorial COGIC — G-4317 Lippincott, Burton, MI 48519 — (810) 232-3828
  • Blessed Sacrament Church — 6340 Roberta, Burton, MI 48509 — (810) 742-6128
  • CenterPoint Church of Burton — 1225 S. Center Rd, Burton, MI 48509 — (810) 743-0000
  • Holy Redeemer Catholic Church — 1227 E. Bristol Rd, Burton, MI 48529 — (810) 348-1245
  • Hurley Prescription Pantry — 2065 S. Center Rd, Burton, MI 48519 — (810) 262-2345

Who to call (N11 & non-emergency numbers)

N11 codes are the "short dial" for community and government services — just dial the number.

  • 2-1-1 — Community Services: Central Michigan 211 (United Way of Genesee County) connects you to food pantries, housing assistance (Shelter of Flint), and utility help (GCCARD).
  • 5-1-1 — Travel & Traffic: MDOT Mi Drive — real-time I-69 / I-475 construction and winter road conditions.
  • 7-1-1 — Relay Service: Michigan Relay for those who are deaf, hard of hearing, or speech-disabled.
  • 8-1-1 — MISS DIG: Michigan's utility safety line. Call at least 3 business days before digging in your yard.
  • 9-1-1 — Emergency: Genesee County 911 — dispatch for Burton Police, Fire, and EMS.
  • 9-8-8 — Crisis Lifeline: connects you to Genesee Health System (the local mental-health authority) for crisis support and behavioral-health urgent care.

Key local non-emergency numbers

  • Burton Police (non-emergency): (810) 742-2542 — crimes not in progress, noise complaints, general info
  • Burton DPW: (810) 742-9230 — potholes, water main breaks, snow removal
  • The Disability Network (in Burton): (810) 742-1800 — advocacy & accessibility support
  • GCCARD (Community Action): (810) 232-2185 — weatherization, senior nutrition (Meals on Wheels), emergency utility help

Addiction & recovery resources

If you are in immediate danger or a medical crisis, call 911 or the National Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988.

You're not struggling alone.

Narcotics.com connects people to free resources, patient-centered guidance, and verified Narcotics Anonymous meetings nationwide — including a dedicated NA meetings page for the City of Burton. Help line: 1-800-934-1582.

Other trusted partners

  • Therapy.com — connects users with licensed therapists nationwide; a searchable directory plus mental-health and therapy resources.
  • Boca Recovery Center — care for substance-use and mental-health disorders with advanced treatment for lasting recovery.
  • Rehab.com — connects individuals and families with trusted treatment providers for substance use, mental health, and behavioral challenges.

Disclaimer: The City of Burton provides these addiction resources for educational purposes. We do not provide direct medical services, and the inclusion of any organization does not imply a formal endorsement. Please consult with a healthcare professional before beginning any treatment program.

content.ordinances:
Burton Code of Ordinances

The City's local laws are collected in the Code of Ordinances, published and kept up to date for the City by American Legal Publishing. The online code is the official, always-current version and includes a search box for finding a specific rule.

  • Browse the full Code of Ordinances

Jump to a section

Each link opens that part of the code on the official American Legal site:

  • Official City Charter — Burton's foundational governing document
  • Title I: General Provisions
  • Title III: Administration — city government and departments
  • Title V: Public Works — streets, utilities, and infrastructure
  • Title VII: Traffic Code — parking, speed, and local traffic rules
  • Title IX: General Regulations
  • Title XI: Business Regulations — business licensing and permits
  • Title XIII: General Offenses — nuisances, noise, animals, and conduct
  • Title XV: Land Usage — zoning, land division, and property use

Certified copies & recent ordinances

The online code is updated after the City Council adopts and codifies an ordinance, so the newest actions may not appear there yet. For a certified copy of an ordinance, or the status of a recent one, contact the City Clerk at City Hall, (810) 743-1500.
